html:
Korea under Japanese rule was the period from 1910 to 1945 when Korea was a colony of the Empire of Japan. It ended the five centuries of the Joseon dynasty.

After beating Russia in 1905, Japan made Korea a protectorate, and in August 1910 it annexed the country outright. A Japanese governor-general ruled with the army and military police.

  • In 1919 the March 1st Movement brought huge peaceful protests for independence. They were crushed, and Japan then allowed a little more freedom of the press.
  • Japan built railways such as the Gyeongbu Line, ports and, in the north, heavy industry, mostly to serve its own economy. After the rice riots of 1918 in Japan, more and more Korean rice was shipped there.
  • Many Koreans moved to Japan and Manchuria. After the Great Kantō earthquake of 1923, mobs in Japan murdered thousands of Koreans.

From the late 1930s Japan tried to erase Korean identity. Korean was pushed out of schools, people had to worship at Shinto shrines and take Japanese-style names, and in the war years hundreds of thousands were taken as labourers and soldiers, and many women were forced into military brothels as "comfort women".

Resistance went on abroad, from a provisional government in Shanghai to guerrillas in Manchuria such as the young Kim Il Sung. Japan's surrender in August 1945 freed Korea, but American and Soviet troops divided it, which led to the Korean War.
sum: Korea under Japanese rule was the period from 1910 to 1945 when Korea was a colony of the Empire of Japan. It ended the five centuries of the Joseon dynasty.
